items.subtype: subject-verb agreement across an intervening prepositional phrase
items.stem: According to the latest forecast, the pattern of pressure changes near the coast ____ before dawn.
items.answer_explanation: The singular head noun pattern takes the singular verb is; the intervening of-phrase does not change the subject.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: is agrees with the singular subject pattern.
distractor_rationales.B: The plural verb are incorrectly agrees with pressure or changes instead of pattern.
distractor_rationales.C: This is a nonfinite fragment and does not provide a finite main verb.
distractor_rationales.D: This repeats the subject and omits the required finite verb construction after the blank.

items.subtype: embedded question with statement word order
items.stem: The map archivist explained ____ during the survey.

options.A: where had the old boundary markers been moved
options.B: where the old boundary markers had been moved
options.D: where did the old boundary markers move

items.answer_explanation: An embedded question uses statement order: subject before the auxiliary, as in where the markers had been moved.

distractor_rationales.A: The auxiliary is inverted as in a direct question, so the embedded clause has the wrong word order.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: the embedded question has the subject before the auxiliary.
distractor_rationales.C: The embedded clause is incomplete because it lacks a finite verb.
distractor_rationales.D: This uses direct-question inversion inside an embedded question.

items.subtype: non-restrictive relative clause with passive predicate
items.stem: The sandstone tablet, ____ during the excavation, is now displayed in the conservation laboratory.
items.answer_explanation: The non-restrictive relative clause needs which as its marker and the passive verb phrase was uncovered.

distractor_rationales.A: What cannot introduce this non-restrictive relative clause.
distractor_rationales.B: Uncovering is the wrong verb form for the required passive predicate.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: which introduces the clause and was uncovered is passive and finite.
distractor_rationales.D: The relative marker and a redundant subject pronoun duplicate the subject.

items.subtype: time clause introduced by when
items.stem: The telescope records extra images ____ the sky becomes clear after sunset.
items.answer_explanation: The time clause requires when followed by a subject and a finite verb: the sky becomes clear.

distractor_rationales.A: During is a preposition and cannot introduce the following finite clause.
distractor_rationales.B: The clause uses a nonfinite form instead of the required finite verb.
distractor_rationales.C: The subject and predicate are incorrectly ordered and the clause is not well formed.
distractor_rationales.D: Correct: when introduces a complete time clause with subject and finite verb.

items.subtype: contrast connector before a noun phrase
items.stem: The alloy remains flexible ____ repeated cooling and heating.
items.answer_explanation: Despite correctly introduces the noun phrase repeated cooling and heating to express contrast.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: despite is followed directly by a noun phrase.
distractor_rationales.B: Although must introduce a finite clause, not the noun phrase that follows.
distractor_rationales.C: In spite requires the preposition of before this noun phrase.
distractor_rationales.D: Despite does not take of; the extra preposition is unnecessary.

items.subtype: past perfect passive before a later past event
items.stem: By the time the survey team arrived, the mineral samples ____ in sealed containers.
items.answer_explanation: The earlier completed event requires past perfect, and the samples receive the action, so the form is had been labeled.

distractor_rationales.A: The participle is malformed; label must be in its past-participial form.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: had been labeled is past perfect passive.
distractor_rationales.C: The active form incorrectly makes the samples perform the labeling.
distractor_rationales.D: The passive auxiliary is missing its required past participle.

items.subtype: causative verb with object plus predicate adjective
items.stem: The monitoring station's new filter made the river water ____ after heavy rainfall.
items.answer_explanation: Make takes an object followed by a bare predicate adjective: made the water clearer.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: clearer is the adjective complement after the object river water.
distractor_rationales.B: Clearly is an adverb, not the required predicate adjective.
distractor_rationales.C: Make does not take to plus the infinitive in this object-complement pattern.
distractor_rationales.D: The -ing form does not function as the required adjective complement here.

items.subtype: reduced passive participial modifier
items.stem: ____ in shaded soil, the seeds germinated slowly after the spring rain.
items.answer_explanation: The seeds receive the action, so a reduced passive modifier uses the past participle planted.

distractor_rationales.A: Having planting is not a valid perfect participial form.
distractor_rationales.B: The active participle incorrectly presents the seeds as doing the planting.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: planted is a reduced passive modifier of the seeds.
distractor_rationales.D: Were planted is a finite clause fragment and cannot modify the subject in this position.

items.subtype: adjective plus enough plus to-infinitive result construction
items.stem: The detector was ____ to register faint signals from the distant star.
items.answer_explanation: Enough follows the adjective in the adjective + enough + to-infinitive construction.

distractor_rationales.A: Enough is placed before the adjective instead of after it.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: sensitive enough licenses the following to-infinitive.
distractor_rationales.C: So normally requires a that-clause for this result construction.
distractor_rationales.D: The following form is not the required to-infinitive construction.

items.subtype: parallel bare infinitives in a three-part list
items.stem: During fieldwork, the geologists had to ____ the slope, record the rock layers, and label the samples.
items.answer_explanation: Had to is followed by a bare infinitive, and measure is parallel with record and label.

distractor_rationales.A: The -ing form is not the bare infinitive required after had to.
distractor_rationales.B: A noun cannot be coordinated with the two verb forms in the list.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: measure is the bare infinitive parallel to record and label.
distractor_rationales.D: The added to creates to to measure after had to.

items.subtype: adjective order inside a complex noun phrase
items.stem: The museum displayed ____ from the coastal excavation.

options.B: a finely work small bronze bowl
options.C: a finely worked old small bronze bowl
options.D: a finely worked small bronze bowl

items.answer_explanation: The participial modifier finely worked precedes the size adjective small, which precedes the material adjective bronze and the noun bowl.

distractor_rationales.A: The modifiers are ordered incorrectly around the participial adjective and material adjective.
distractor_rationales.B: Work is the wrong part-of-speech form; the participial modifier is worked.
distractor_rationales.C: The unnecessary adjective old adds an extraneous element to the planned noun phrase.
distractor_rationales.D: Correct: the modifier order is finely worked, small, bronze, bowl.

items.subtype: subject-auxiliary inversion after only after
items.stem: Only after the glacier retreated ____ the researchers discover the buried lake.
items.answer_explanation: Fronted only after triggers subject-auxiliary inversion: did the researchers discover.

distractor_rationales.A: The inverted auxiliary lacks the required subject.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: the auxiliary precedes the subject after fronted only after.
distractor_rationales.C: The subject remains before the auxiliary, so inversion is absent.
distractor_rationales.D: This is a nonfinite and incorrectly ordered fragment.

items.subtype: there plus be with a plural postposed noun phrase
items.stem: Near the wind-eroded ridge, ____ several narrow channels after the storm.
items.answer_explanation: The existential construction uses there, and the plural postposed noun channels requires were.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: there were agrees with the plural noun channels.
distractor_rationales.B: It is a referring pronoun and does not form the required existential construction.
distractor_rationales.C: The singular verb was does not agree with plural channels.
distractor_rationales.D: The expletive there is missing.

items.subtype: plural pronoun reference for a coordinated human subject
items.stem: The mentor and the apprentice recorded their measurements before ____ submitted the report.
items.answer_explanation: The coordinated subjects are plural, so the following subject pronoun is they.

distractor_rationales.A: He is singular and cannot refer to both the mentor and the apprentice.
distractor_rationales.B: Them is an object pronoun, not the subject of submitted.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: they is the plural subject pronoun for the two people.
distractor_rationales.D: Their is possessive and cannot function as the subject here.

items.subtype: noun required as the object of a preposition
items.stem: The accuracy of the experiment depends on ____ of the instrument before each trial.
items.answer_explanation: The preposition on requires a noun phrase, and the noun calibration is the head of the phrase.

distractor_rationales.A: A verb phrase cannot serve as the required noun object of on in this construction.
distractor_rationales.B: The noun and adjective are in the wrong order.
distractor_rationales.C: The noun head calibration is missing.
distractor_rationales.D: Correct: the careful calibration is a complete noun phrase after on.

items.subtype: singular head noun in an of-phrase subject
items.sentence: The calibration of the instruments record stable readings during each trial.

marked_parts.A: The calibration of the instruments record

items.answer_explanation: Calibration is the singular head of the subject noun phrase, so the main verb must be records.

items.subtype: adjective required before a plural head noun
items.sentence: The engineer selected several durability bearings for the test rig.
items.answer_explanation: The noun bearings needs an adjective modifier, so durable, not the noun durability, is required.

items.subtype: simple past main verb after a past perfect subordinate clause
items.sentence: After the lighthouse crew had repaired the lamp, the keeper records the inspection details.

marked_parts.A: After the lighthouse crew had repaired the lamp,

items.answer_explanation: The past perfect clause establishes a past time frame, so the main verb should be simple past recorded.

items.subtype: adjective-governed preposition in an interested-in phrase
items.sentence: The archivist was deeply interested on maps from the coastal archive.

marked_parts.D: on maps from the coastal archive.

items.answer_explanation: The established adjective-preposition collocation is interested in, not interested on.

items.subtype: gerund complements coordinated after a training preposition
items.sentence: The workshop focuses on carve wood and shaping clay for architectural models.
items.answer_explanation: The preposition on takes gerund complements, and carving must be parallel with shaping.

items.subtype: adjective complement after responsible for
items.sentence: The engineer is responsible to the mountain station's ventilation system.
items.answer_explanation: When responsible means having duty for something, it is followed by the preposition for.

items.subtype: subject relative pronoun for a human antecedent
items.sentence: The surveyor which mapped the village explained the boundary changes.
items.answer_explanation: The antecedent surveyor is a person and is the subject of mapped, so the relative marker should be who.

items.subtype: participial adjective before a material adjective in a noun phrase
items.sentence: The museum restored a bronze finely decorated vessel from the collection.
items.minimal_correction: bronze finely decorated vessel → finely decorated bronze vessel
items.answer_explanation: The participial modifier finely decorated precedes the material adjective bronze in the noun phrase.

items.subtype: singular head noun with an of-phrase interrupter
items.sentence: The collection of oral histories contain vivid accounts of migration from the valley.

marked_parts.A: The collection of oral histories contain

items.answer_explanation: The singular head noun collection controls agreement; the plural noun histories is inside an of-phrase.

items.subtype: removal of a redundant coordinator after an although clause
items.sentence: Although the route was steep, but the hikers reached the summit before noon.
items.answer_explanation: Although already introduces the subordinate contrast clause, so the additional coordinator but is unnecessary.

items.subtype: passive transitive verb requiring a by-agent phrase
items.sentence: The manuscript was carefully restored the librarian last year.
items.minimal_correction: restored the librarian → restored by the librarian
items.answer_explanation: In the passive construction, the agent must be introduced by by: restored by the librarian.

items.subtype: past participle after a perfect auxiliary
items.sentence: The team has carefully prepared the samples that they have record.
items.answer_explanation: The auxiliary have requires the past participle recorded.

items.subtype: pronoun without an explicit antecedent
items.sentence: It was placed beside the research equipment after the technician finished.
items.answer_explanation: The sentence supplies no antecedent for It; an explicit noun such as The sensor is needed.

items.subtype: adjective required as a noun modifier after an article
items.sentence: The lecturer presented a scientifically overview of public water systems.
items.answer_explanation: The noun overview requires the adjective scientific as its modifier, not the adverb scientifically.

items.subtype: comparative adjective without a redundant more marker
items.sentence: The northern route is considerably more shorter than the southern route during winter.

marked_parts.C: more shorter than the southern route

items.answer_explanation: Shorter is already a comparative form, so the redundant more must be removed.

items.subtype: because clause rather than because-of before a finite clause
items.sentence: The plants grew slowly during the trial because of the soil remained unusually cold.

marked_parts.D: of the soil remained unusually cold.

items.minimal_correction: because of the soil remained unusually cold → because the soil remained unusually cold
items.answer_explanation: A finite clause follows because, whereas because of must be followed by a noun phrase.

items.subtype: there-be agreement with a plural postposed noun phrase
items.sentence: There is several balconies along the theater's upper gallery.
items.answer_explanation: The plural postposed noun balconies requires the plural form are in the existential construction.

items.subtype: embedded why-question with statement word order
items.sentence: The analyst could not determine why did the values change after calibration.
items.minimal_correction: why did the values change → why the values changed
items.answer_explanation: The clause after determine is an embedded question and therefore uses statement order.

items.subtype: adjective-governed dependent-on preposition
items.sentence: The strength of the coating is dependent of temperature and humidity.
items.answer_explanation: The established collocation is dependent on, so of is the wrong preposition.

items.subtype: gerund coordination after recommends
items.sentence: The committee recommends mapping the district and to revise its zoning plan.
items.answer_explanation: The complements coordinated after recommends should be parallel gerund phrases: mapping and revising.

items.subtype: adverb required to modify a verb
items.sentence: The seedlings grew rapid under the controlled lamps.
items.answer_explanation: The verb grew requires the adverb rapidly to describe how the seedlings grew.

items.subtype: reduced passive modifier before a finite passive predicate
items.sentence: The panels, having built from recycled glass, were tested for strength.
items.minimal_correction: having built from recycled glass → built from recycled glass
items.answer_explanation: The panels receive the action, so the reduced modifier must be passive: built from recycled glass.

items.subtype: simple past main verb after a past perfect passive clause
items.sentence: After the bridge had been inspected, engineers approves the repair plan.

marked_parts.A: After the bridge had been inspected,

items.answer_explanation: The completed inspection places the following event in the past, so the main verb should be approved.

items.subtype: countable quantifier before a plural count noun
items.sentence: The questionnaire included much responses from first-year students.
items.answer_explanation: Responses is a plural count noun, so it requires the quantifier many rather than much.

items.subtype: adverb required to modify an adverb
items.sentence: The seedlings grew surprising quickly in the greenhouse.
items.answer_explanation: The word modifies the adverb quickly, so it must be the adverb surprisingly.

items.subtype: subject-verb agreement across an intervening prepositional phrase
items.stem: The leaves of the desert plant ___ during the dry season.
items.answer_explanation: The past-tense verb agrees with the plural subject leaves and the completed-time context.

distractor_rationales.A: The present form does not match the completed-time context.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: wilted agrees with leaves in the past-tense clause.
distractor_rationales.C: The singular present form does not agree with leaves.
distractor_rationales.D: The participle cannot serve as the finite verb here.

items.subtype: embedded question with statement word order
items.stem: Researchers have not determined ___ the ancient temple was built.
items.answer_explanation: An embedded question uses statement order: when the temple was built.

distractor_rationales.A: Inversion is not used in an embedded question.
distractor_rationales.B: Do-inversion is not used after determined.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: when introduces the embedded clause with statement order.
distractor_rationales.D: That cannot introduce this embedded question meaningfully.

items.subtype: restrictive relative clause with object relative marker
items.stem: The wetlands ___ the university restored now attract many birds.
items.answer_explanation: That is the object relative marker in the restrictive clause.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: that replaces the object of restored.
distractor_rationales.B: The extra subject creates a double-object structure.
distractor_rationales.C: The extra they makes the relative clause ungrammatical.
distractor_rationales.D: The participle does not form the intended finite relative clause.

items.subtype: conditional clause with a finite subordinate clause
items.stem: ___ the storm weakens, coastal residents will remain indoors.
items.answer_explanation: If introduces the condition for the result clause.

distractor_rationales.A: Because expresses cause, not the stated condition.
distractor_rationales.B: Although expresses contrast rather than a condition.
distractor_rationales.C: Unless reverses the intended condition.
distractor_rationales.D: Correct: if introduces the conditional subordinate clause.

items.subtype: contrast connector followed by a finite clause
items.stem: The proposal was expensive, ___ the council approved it.
items.answer_explanation: But correctly coordinates two contrasting independent clauses.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: but signals the contrast.
distractor_rationales.B: Because gives a cause and cannot coordinate these ideas as intended.
distractor_rationales.C: Unless introduces a condition.
distractor_rationales.D: So that introduces purpose or result.

items.subtype: passive voice in a completed research process
items.stem: Before publication, the alloy samples ___ by three independent laboratories.
items.answer_explanation: Had been tested expresses a completed passive process before publication.

distractor_rationales.A: The simple past omits the earlier-completion relationship.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: had been tested is past perfect passive.
distractor_rationales.C: The active present perfect has the wrong voice and time.
distractor_rationales.D: The progressive active form has the wrong voice.

items.subtype: causative verb followed by object and predicate adjective
items.stem: The new trees will make the avenue ___.
items.answer_explanation: Make takes an object followed by a predicate adjective describing it.

distractor_rationales.A: The bare noun/verb form is not the required predicate adjective.
distractor_rationales.B: The participle does not fit the selected complement frame.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: shady is the predicate adjective after make the avenue.
distractor_rationales.D: This adverb cannot function as the predicate complement.

items.subtype: reduced passive relative clause with a past participle
items.stem: The fragments ___ in the crater were preserved for analysis.
items.answer_explanation: To discover is the infinitive form required by the intended reduced construction.

distractor_rationales.A: The active participle gives the fragments an implausible agent role.
distractor_rationales.B: The past participle creates a different reduced passive reading.
distractor_rationales.C: A finite clause cannot fill this reduced phrase position.
distractor_rationales.D: Correct for the planned infinitive construction.

items.subtype: so plus adjective licensing a result that-clause
items.stem: The chamber was ___ that even a whisper could be recorded clearly.
items.answer_explanation: Such quiet is the planned degree expression licensing the following that result clause.

distractor_rationales.A: So normally requires an adjective phrase, not the planned noun phrase construction.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct for the selected such-plus-noun result construction.
distractor_rationales.C: An adverb cannot serve as the complement of was here.
distractor_rationales.D: As quiet requires a comparison complement.

items.subtype: not only plus coordinated parallel verb phrases
items.stem: The exhibit not only informs visitors but also ___.
items.answer_explanation: The two coordinated complements are parallel finite verb phrases.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: entertains them parallels informs visitors.
distractor_rationales.B: The participle is not parallel to the finite verb.
distractor_rationales.C: A noun is not parallel to the verb phrase.
distractor_rationales.D: The infinitive is not parallel to the finite verb.

items.subtype: appositive noun phrase after a proper noun
items.stem: Maya Chen, ___, presented the findings at the conference.
items.answer_explanation: The appositive noun phrase follows the proper name and identifies Maya Chen.

distractor_rationales.A: The adjective is misplaced after the noun in this phrase.
distractor_rationales.B: The word order does not form an appositive noun phrase.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: a respected sociolinguist is a well-formed appositive.
distractor_rationales.D: The determiner and noun order is incorrect.

items.subtype: subject-auxiliary inversion after a fronted negative adverbial
items.stem: Never before ___ such a significant amendment been proposed.
items.answer_explanation: The fronted negative adverbial requires inversion of the auxiliary and subject.

distractor_rationales.A: The auxiliary lacks its subject.
distractor_rationales.B: The inserted phrase disrupts the required inversion.
distractor_rationales.C: It adds a subject that is not part of the intended clause.
distractor_rationales.D: Correct: it has follows the fronted negative adverbial in the planned order.

items.subtype: there plus be with a postposed plural noun phrase
items.stem: There ___ several underground streams beneath the valley.
items.answer_explanation: The plural postposed noun phrase streams requires are.

distractor_rationales.A: Is does not agree with the plural noun phrase.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: are agrees with several streams.
distractor_rationales.C: The bare form cannot be the finite verb here.
distractor_rationales.D: The participle cannot serve as the finite verb.

items.subtype: quantifier selected for an uncountable academic noun
items.stem: The report provides ___ information about regional employment trends.
items.answer_explanation: Information is uncountable, so much is the appropriate quantifier.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: much modifies the uncountable noun information.
distractor_rationales.B: Many modifies plural count nouns.
distractor_rationales.C: Few modifies plural count nouns.
distractor_rationales.D: Several modifies plural count nouns.

items.subtype: adverb required to modify a following finite verb
items.stem: The filter operates ___ when the input signal contains background noise.
items.answer_explanation: An adverb is required to modify the finite verb operates.

distractor_rationales.A: The adjective cannot directly modify operates.
distractor_rationales.B: The noun cannot modify the verb.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: efficiently is the adverb modifying operates.
distractor_rationales.D: The comparative adjective lacks a comparison and the required adverbial function.

items.subtype: article before a singular count noun
items.sentence: An ecosystem supports many forms of life.
items.answer_explanation: The article an correctly precedes the singular count noun ecosystem.

items.subtype: simple past in a dated historical sequence
items.sentence: The railway opened the mountain route in 1898.
items.answer_explanation: The dated event correctly uses the simple past.

items.subtype: adjective modifying a research noun
items.sentence: The study reports significant changes in memory.
items.answer_explanation: The adjective significant correctly modifies the noun changes.

items.subtype: quantifier with a plural count noun
items.sentence: Several methods improve the harvest yield.
items.minimal_correction: D: the harvest yield → the harvest yields
items.answer_explanation: The planned correction makes the quantified count noun plural.

items.subtype: parallel gerund phrases after a coordinator
items.sentence: The course emphasizes reading critically and writing clearly.
items.answer_explanation: The two gerund phrases are parallel after emphasizes.

items.subtype: adjective complement after a linking verb
items.sentence: The plateau appears stable during the dry season.
items.answer_explanation: Appears correctly takes the predicate adjective stable.

items.subtype: gerund as the object of a preposition
items.sentence: Scientists are committed to protecting the coral reef.
items.answer_explanation: The preposition to is correctly followed by the gerund protecting.

items.subtype: relative pronoun as the subject of a restrictive clause
items.sentence: The arch that supports the roof was recently repaired.
items.minimal_correction: D: was recently repaired → was recently repaired
items.answer_explanation: That correctly serves as the subject of the restrictive relative clause.

items.subtype: adverb modifying a participle
items.sentence: The rapidly moving clouds covered the horizon.
items.answer_explanation: Rapidly is the adverb modifying moving.

items.subtype: preposition selected for a noun phrase
items.sentence: Investors are concerned about the sudden change.
items.answer_explanation: Concerned correctly combines with the preposition about.

items.subtype: pronoun agreement with a singular antecedent
items.sentence: Each participant submitted their questionnaire before leaving.
items.minimal_correction: C: their questionnaire → his or her questionnaire
items.answer_explanation: The singular antecedent each participant requires a singular pronoun in the locked construction.

items.subtype: parallel noun phrases after both and
items.sentence: The survey measured both public trust and policy awareness.
items.minimal_correction: D: and policy awareness → and policy awareness
items.answer_explanation: Both coordinates the parallel noun phrases public trust and policy awareness.

items.subtype: passive voice with an object receiving an action
items.sentence: The vaccine was tested on volunteers before approval.
items.answer_explanation: The vaccine correctly receives the action in the passive construction.

items.subtype: adjective phrase in postmodifier position
items.sentence: The poems written during exile reveal a new style.
items.minimal_correction: B: written during exile → written during exile
items.answer_explanation: The participial adjective phrase correctly follows and modifies poems.

items.subtype: present participle in a reduced active clause
items.sentence: Using infrared sensors, the robot avoids obstacles.
items.answer_explanation: Using correctly introduces a reduced active clause whose understood subject is the robot.

items.subtype: definite article for a uniquely identified institution
items.sentence: The court published its decision on Monday.
items.minimal_correction: D: on Monday → on the Monday
items.answer_explanation: The planned correction supplies the definite article in the marked institutional time phrase.

items.subtype: comparative adjective with than
items.sentence: The second estimate is more precise than the first.
items.minimal_correction: A: The second estimate → The second estimate
items.answer_explanation: More precise correctly forms the comparative with than.

items.subtype: verb governed by an infinitive complement
items.sentence: The device allows operators to adjust the pressure.
items.answer_explanation: Allow correctly takes an object followed by an infinitive complement.

items.subtype: parallel finite verbs coordinated by and
items.sentence: The conductor raised the baton and began the performance.
items.minimal_correction: C: raised the baton and began → raised the baton and began
items.answer_explanation: Raised and began are parallel finite verbs coordinated by and.

items.subtype: noun required as the object of a preposition
items.sentence: The artifact provides evidence of early settlement.
items.answer_explanation: Settlement is the noun required after the preposition of.

items.subtype: whose for a possessive relative relationship
items.sentence: The star whose spectrum changed was observed again.
items.answer_explanation: Whose correctly marks the possessive relationship between star and spectrum.

items.subtype: although introducing a finite concessive clause
items.sentence: Although costs increased, the program continued to expand.
items.answer_explanation: Although correctly introduces the finite concessive clause.

items.subtype: past perfect before a later past event
items.sentence: The patient had recovered before the physician arrived.
items.answer_explanation: Had recovered correctly marks the earlier of the two past events.

items.subtype: few with a plural count noun
items.sentence: Few residents opposed the construction plan.
items.minimal_correction: D: the construction plan → the construction plans
items.answer_explanation: The planned correction makes the quantified count noun plural.

items.subtype: infinitive of purpose before a main clause
items.sentence: To reduce emissions, the city expanded its solar program.
items.minimal_correction: A: To reduce emissions → To reduce emissions
items.answer_explanation: The infinitive phrase correctly expresses the purpose of the main clause.

items.subtype: subject-verb agreement across an intervening prepositional phrase
items.stem: The orbit of several newly discovered planets ___ unusually stable.
items.answer_explanation: The singular head noun orbit requires the singular verb remains.

distractor_rationales.A: Remain agrees with the nearby plural noun planets, not the subject head.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: orbit is singular.
distractor_rationales.C: The participle cannot serve as the finite predicate.
distractor_rationales.D: Has remain uses an incorrect participle form.

items.subtype: embedded question with noninverted word order
items.stem: Researchers are uncertain whether the pottery fragments ___ from the coastal settlement.
items.answer_explanation: An embedded whether-question uses statement word order: subject followed by the finite verb.

distractor_rationales.A: Inversion with did is not used in this embedded question.
distractor_rationales.B: The auxiliary is misplaced and the clause is ungrammatical.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: the fragments originated there.
distractor_rationales.D: This is not a complete finite clause.

items.subtype: restrictive relative pronoun as object
items.stem: The researcher cataloged the fern species ___ the expedition had collected.
items.answer_explanation: That correctly introduces a restrictive relative clause and functions as its object.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: that is the object of had collected.
distractor_rationales.B: What cannot follow an antecedent noun in this construction.
distractor_rationales.C: They creates an extra subject and leaves the object missing.
distractor_rationales.D: Which them contains a redundant object.

items.subtype: second conditional clause with full subordinate-clause structure
items.stem: If the city ___ the subsidy, more households would install efficient heating systems.
items.answer_explanation: The second conditional uses a simple past form in the if-clause and would plus base verb in the result.

distractor_rationales.A: The present tense does not form the intended second conditional.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: increased pairs with would install.
distractor_rationales.C: Will is not normally used in this if-clause.
distractor_rationales.D: The progressive form is not required and changes the construction.

items.subtype: concessive relation requiring a prepositional connector before a noun phrase
items.stem: ___ its low density, the alloy withstands considerable pressure.
items.answer_explanation: Despite is followed directly by a noun phrase and expresses concession.

distractor_rationales.A: Although requires a finite clause, not this noun phrase.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: despite its low density.
distractor_rationales.C: Despite of is not the standard prepositional form.
distractor_rationales.D: Because expresses cause rather than concession.

items.subtype: passive voice in a finite main clause
items.stem: The storm system ___ by satellite instruments before it reached the coast.
items.answer_explanation: The system receives the action, so the finite passive was tracked is required.

distractor_rationales.A: Was tracking gives the subject an agentive meaning.
distractor_rationales.B: Tracked is active and lacks an expressed agent.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: the system was tracked.
distractor_rationales.D: Tracking is a nonfinite fragment here.

items.subtype: causative make followed by object and adjective complement
items.stem: The new park design made the narrow corridor ___ and safer for pedestrians.
items.answer_explanation: Make takes an object followed by a bare adjective complement; wider is coordinated with safer.

distractor_rationales.A: Make does not take a to-infinitive complement in this frame.
distractor_rationales.B: The participle is not parallel with safer.
distractor_rationales.C: Widened suggests a passive result and is not coordinated with safer.
distractor_rationales.D: Correct: made the corridor wider and safer.

items.subtype: reduced passive relative clause with a past participle
items.stem: The fibers ___ with a protective coating retain their strength after repeated washing and drying.
items.answer_explanation: Treated is a reduced passive relative clause modifying fibers: fibers that were treated.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: treated means that were treated.
distractor_rationales.B: Treating gives the fibers an incorrect active role.
distractor_rationales.C: Were treated creates a second finite verb in the noun phrase.
distractor_rationales.D: Having treat has an incorrect participle form.

items.subtype: so plus adjective licensing a result that-clause
items.stem: The memory task was so demanding that several participants, after practicing for weeks, ___ unable to finish it.
items.answer_explanation: So demanding that introduces a result clause whose finite predicate is were unable.

distractor_rationales.A: More unable is an unnecessary and awkward degree form.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: participants were unable to finish.
distractor_rationales.C: Being is nonfinite and cannot complete the clause.
distractor_rationales.D: Had been to does not provide the required predicate.

items.subtype: not only but also with coordinated finite verbs
items.stem: The software not only records performances but also ___ background noise automatically.
items.answer_explanation: Not only records but also filters coordinates two finite verbs with the same subject.

distractor_rationales.A: Filtering is not parallel with the finite verb records.
distractor_rationales.B: The to-infinitive is not parallel with records.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: records and filters are coordinated finite verbs.
distractor_rationales.D: The past tense breaks the intended present-tense coordination.

items.subtype: appositive noun phrase in post-subject position
items.stem: Marie Curie, a pioneer in radioactivity research, ___ two Nobel Prizes.
items.answer_explanation: The appositive is parenthetical, so the sentence needs the finite verb received.

distractor_rationales.A: Awarding is nonfinite and lacks a main verb.
distractor_rationales.B: Was award has an incorrect passive form.
distractor_rationales.C: Her award is a noun phrase, not a predicate.
distractor_rationales.D: Correct: Curie received two prizes.

items.subtype: elliptical conditional inversion with had
items.stem: Had the reef restoration project ___ earlier, the damaged habitat might have recovered before winter.
items.answer_explanation: Had plus the past participle forms an inverted past-perfect conditional: had begun.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: had begun is the inverted form of if the project had begun.
distractor_rationales.B: Beginning cannot follow had.
distractor_rationales.C: The inverted clause does not take an extra subject it.
distractor_rationales.D: Been begin uses an incorrect participle.

items.subtype: there plus be with a plural postverbal noun phrase
items.stem: There ___ several blank areas on the early map of the northern coast.
items.answer_explanation: The plural postverbal noun phrase areas requires are in this existential construction.

distractor_rationales.A: Is is singular and does not agree with areas.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: there are several blank areas.
distractor_rationales.C: Being is nonfinite.
distractor_rationales.D: Has does not form the existential construction here.

items.subtype: quantifier compatible with an uncountable noun
items.stem: The recipe requires ___ additional information about the nutritional content of the grain.
items.answer_explanation: Information is uncountable, so some is the compatible quantifier.

distractor_rationales.A: Many modifies countable plural nouns.
distractor_rationales.B: Few also modifies countable plural nouns.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: some information.
distractor_rationales.D: Several requires a countable plural noun.

items.subtype: adverb required to modify a finite verb
items.stem: The archivist explained that the fragile documents must be handled ___ during the transfer.
items.answer_explanation: Carefully is the adverb modifying handled.

distractor_rationales.A: Careful is an adjective, not the required adverb.
distractor_rationales.B: Carefulness is a noun.
distractor_rationales.C: Care is a noun or verb and cannot modify handled here.
distractor_rationales.D: Correct: handled carefully.

items.subtype: indefinite article before a consonant-initial noun
items.sentence: A architect measured the vaulted entrance before the renovation began.
items.answer_explanation: The consonant letter a is pronounced with an initial vowel sound, so the article must be an.

items.subtype: adjective required before a head noun
items.sentence: The region experienced a dramatically temperature shift during the afternoon.
items.answer_explanation: Dramatic is the adjective required to modify temperature; dramatically is an adverb.

items.subtype: simple past finite verb in a completed historical sequence
items.sentence: The clinic introduced the screening program after it identify the main risk factors.
items.answer_explanation: The completed past event requires the simple past identified.

items.subtype: parallel gerund complements in a coordinated list
items.sentence: The course emphasizes reading technical articles, analyzing evidence, and to present findings clearly.
items.answer_explanation: The three complements after emphasizes must use parallel gerund forms.

items.subtype: adjective object complement after find
items.sentence: The court found the new evidence convincing for the jury.
items.answer_explanation: In this frame, the adjective convincing takes to before the recipient of the persuasion.

items.subtype: present participle in a reduced active clause
items.sentence: The buses traveling along the old route, carrying commuters into the city each morning.
items.minimal_correction: The buses travel along the old route, carrying commuters into the city each morning.
items.answer_explanation: The sentence needs a finite main verb; traveling alone leaves the subject without a predicate.

items.subtype: although introducing a finite concessive clause
items.sentence: Despite the market was unstable, investors continued to purchase municipal bonds.
items.answer_explanation: A finite clause requires although, whereas despite must be followed by a noun phrase or gerund.

items.subtype: relative pronoun as the object of a preposition
items.sentence: The plant is one of the species with whom the botanist has worked for years.

marked_parts.D: the botanist has worked for years

items.answer_explanation: Which refers to the plant species; whom is used for people.

items.subtype: subject-verb agreement across an intervening modifier
items.sentence: The pattern of clouds over the mountain indicate an approaching storm.
items.answer_explanation: The singular head noun pattern requires indicates.

items.subtype: quantifier compatible with a countable plural noun
items.sentence: Only much of the dietary samples contained enough iron for the analysis.
items.answer_explanation: Samples is a countable plural noun, so many, not much, is required.

items.subtype: noun required as the head of a prepositional object
items.sentence: The lecturer discussed the historical develop of the regional dialect.
items.answer_explanation: The premodifier historical requires the noun development as the head of the phrase.

items.subtype: passive participle after a finite form of be
items.sentence: The components were assembling in a sealed chamber to prevent contamination.
items.answer_explanation: The components receive the action, so be must be followed by the passive participle assembled.

items.subtype: parallel noun phrases after not only but also
items.sentence: The proposal addresses not only traffic congestion but also should improve pedestrian safety.
items.answer_explanation: The two objects of addresses must be parallel noun phrases: traffic congestion and pedestrian safety.

items.subtype: gerund as the complement of a preposition
items.sentence: The analyst succeeded in predict the quarterly trend despite limited data.
items.answer_explanation: The preposition in takes a gerund complement, predicting.

items.subtype: comparative adjective required by than
items.sentence: The eastern plateau is high than the valley during the dry season.
items.answer_explanation: Than requires the comparative form higher.

items.subtype: adjective order inside a noun phrase
items.sentence: The museum displayed a clay ancient vessel from the excavation.
items.minimal_correction: an ancient clay vessel from the excavation
items.answer_explanation: The age adjective precedes the material adjective: an ancient clay vessel.

items.subtype: singular pronoun agreement with an indefinite antecedent
items.sentence: Each storyteller adapted their account to suit the audience.
items.answer_explanation: In the locked traditional agreement pattern, singular each requires a singular pronoun.

items.subtype: predicate adjective after a linking verb
items.sentence: The amendment appears in constitutional after the court's review.
items.answer_explanation: Appear takes the predicate adjective directly; the inserted preposition in is not part of the linking-verb frame.

items.subtype: adverb required to modify a research verb
items.sentence: The librarian organized the archived manuscripts methodical.
items.answer_explanation: The verb organized is modified by the adverb methodically, not the adjective methodical.

items.subtype: infinitive of purpose after a finite verb
items.sentence: The volunteers collected water samples monitor pollution levels in the wetland.
items.answer_explanation: The infinitive marker to is required before the purpose verb monitor.

items.subtype: fixed preposition collocation after benefit
items.sentence: The observatory benefits from clear skies and benefits to precise measurements.
items.answer_explanation: Benefit takes the preposition from when it means to gain an advantage from something.

items.subtype: parallel finite verbs in a coordinated predicate
items.sentence: The conductor rehearsed the ensemble and checking the balance of the brass section.

marked_parts.D: the balance of the brass section

items.answer_explanation: Rehearsed and checked are coordinated finite past-tense verbs with the same subject.

items.subtype: singular agreement after each
items.sentence: Each of the historic vehicles require careful maintenance.
items.answer_explanation: The subject each is singular, so the verb must be requires.

items.subtype: past perfect for the earlier of two past events
items.sentence: The geologists realized that the glacier melted before they had reached the valley.
items.answer_explanation: The earlier melting event takes the past perfect had melted relative to the later realization.

items.subtype: postpositive adjective phrase following an indefinite pronoun
items.sentence: The treatment plant needs something useful for removing sediment efficiently.
items.minimal_correction: needs something to remove sediment efficiently
items.answer_explanation: The adjective useful does not express the intended function; the unique grammatical repair is the purpose infinitive to remove.
